BI01.bill_description: Grants Ainu co-official status in willing municipalities, funds language schools, and opens a claims process for ancestral land.
BI01.case_for: It keeps a living language in daily use while there are still fluent speakers to teach it.
BI01.case_against: It divides towns along ethnic lines.
BI01.middle_ground: A language-school fund with no land process.

positions.cue_text: Heritage matters, but this needs more thought.
Our ancestors' tongue returns to its own land.
Rural towns cannot fund another mandate.
Our districts never asked for this.
Good intentions, poorly drafted law.
One Yezo, one people, one law.

BI02.bill_description: Guarantees direct payments to rice and dairy farmers whenever market prices fall below a national floor.
BI02.case_for: It keeps family farms afloat through bad years so the island does not depend on imported food.
BI02.case_against: It rewards big farms and raises prices.
BI02.main_risk: Overproduction paid for by the treasury.
BI02.middle_ground: A temporary support fund for bad years.

positions.cue_text: Those who feed us deserve stability.
The land sustains us; we sustain it.
Yezo cannot let the farms fail.
We'll see what our growers say.
Price floors only postpone the reckoning.
Government dependency will undermine us.

BI03.bill_description: Creates deregulated investment zones around Sapporo, Tomakomai, and Hakodate with streamlined permits and labor rules.
BI03.who_gains: New employers and the workers they hire
BI03.case_for: It brings employers and jobs to towns that have been losing both, under rules that are clear from day one.
BI03.case_against: It carves out a second set of rules for the rich.
BI03.main_risk: A race to the bottom on labor protections.
BI03.middle_ground: A single pilot zone with a review.

positions.cue_text: Loosening rules invites exploitation.
Sapporo reels in profits, and our people are on the hook.
Show us what the farm towns get.
Not enough zones in our communities.
Open the doors and let Yezo compete!
Build factories, build jobs, build now.

BI04.bill_description: Moves up the Sapporo extension timeline and funds freight upgrades between Aomori and Hakodate.
BI04.who_gains: Commuters, freight shippers and tourist towns
BI04.case_for: It ties the north to the rest of the country faster and gives freight a reliable route.
BI04.case_against: It spends billions to save minutes.
BI04.main_risk: Cost overruns on tunnels and track.
BI04.middle_ground: Freight upgrades first, with passengers in a second step.

positions.cue_text: Rail over roads is the gentler path.
Connect the north without leaving it behind.
The Shinkansen keeps the city and inaka together.
Long overdue.
This will undermine our domestic ferry companies.
You are throwing limited funds into a hole.

BI05.bill_description: Funds new patrol vessels and radar stations across the Chishima islands in response to Russian exercises offshore.
BI05.who_gains: Island residents and coast guard crews
BI05.case_for: It protects island residents and fishing crews in waters where a neighbor tests our resolve.
BI05.case_against: It provokes a neighbor we need.

positions.cue_text: Weapons invite the very danger they fear.
Chishima needs fishery harbors, not warships.
Our fishermen deserve protection at sea.
Reasonable, if the islands get the contracts.
Security matters; so does the budget.
Moscow must see we will not bend.

BI06.bill_description: Creates five-year work visas for foreign workers in agriculture, fisheries, construction, and tourism.
BI06.who_pays: Local workers whose wages could slip
BI06.case_for: It fills jobs that are going empty on farms, in harbors and on building sites.
BI06.main_risk: Exploitation of workers and strained housing.
BI06.middle_ground: A smaller visa quota for seasonal work only.

positions.cue_text: Yezo does not have enough support for them, yet.
We are here, too. Invest in our people.
Our harvests rot without more hands.
Our hotels and boats need workers.
A shrinking nation cannot close its doors.
Yezo jobs belong to Yezo workers!

BI07.bill_name: Grid Resilience and Renewable Energy Act
BI07.bill_description: After the Iburi earthquake blackout, funds grid interconnection and local wind and geothermal generation.
BI07.who_gains: Rural towns and households that lost power
BI07.case_for: It keeps the lights on after the next quake and builds power that does not depend on imports.
BI07.case_against: It buys power that costs more.

positions.cue_text: Never again should Yezo go dark.
Clean power, built by local hands.
Candlelight does not work for the city or our inaka.
Resilience first; our towns went dark.
Let utilities compete and build to real needs, not bureaucratic whims.
Another blank check dressed as green policy.

BI08.bill_description: Raises the consumption tax from 8% to 10%, with all new revenue earmarked for pensions and elder care.
BI08.case_for: It pays for pensions and care as the population ages, instead of passing the bill to the next generation.
BI08.case_against: It taxes the poor to pay for the old.
BI08.middle_ground: A tax on the largest incomes.

positions.cue_text: Invest our wealth into elders and care.
Our aging villages need help and care.
Painful, but our pensioners come first.
Too many uneven results and impacts.
More spending thrown around without results.
Hands off our shopping streets and farmers!

BI09.bill_description: Transfers revenue-raising and budget authority to the Hokkaido, Aomori, and Chishima prefectural assemblies.
BI09.case_for: It lets regions set budgets for their own needs instead of waiting on the capital.
BI09.case_against: It lets wealthy areas keep their wealth.
BI09.main_risk: Gaps between rich and poor prefectures.
BI09.middle_ground: Devolving one budget line as a trial.

positions.cue_text: Local power, yes, but who guards fairness?
Decisions belong where people actually live.
Sapporo bureaucrats don't know our valleys.
Our towns, our money, our choices.
Three budgets triple  waste and triple the lack of accountability.
We'll wait to see who really gains.

BI10.bill_description: Requires parties to make efforts to field equal numbers of men and women as candidates.
BI10.who_pays: Candidates who might be passed over
BI10.case_for: It gives voters a fairer choice of candidates and opens politics to people long kept out.
BI10.middle_ground: Voluntary party targets with public reports.

positions.cue_text: Wisdom has never belonged to one gender.
Our communities decide who represents them.
Farm women have always carried half.
Fair enough, as long as it's voluntary.
Why not a quota on ideas in here?
Parties choose candidates. Talk to your selection committee.

BI11.bill_description: Establishes a standing Yezo–Japan commission on strait shipping, shared fisheries, and ferry customs.
BI11.who_gains: Ferry operators, fishers and border towns
BI11.case_for: It gives both sides of the strait one place to settle shipping, fishing and customs problems before they grow.
BI11.case_against: It hands control of our waters to talks.
BI11.main_risk: A commission with no power to settle anything.
BI11.middle_ground: A yearly meeting with no standing body.

positions.cue_text: Good neighbors share their waters.
Tokyo's hand reaches north again.
Fine for Aomori; unclear for us.
Ferries and fish, sensible enough.
Cooperation, yes; creeping reunification, no.
Closer to Japan, stronger together.

BI12.bill_description: Moves Supreme Court nominations from the Cabinet to an independent appointments commission.
BI12.who_gains: Courts that want distance from politics
BI12.case_for: It keeps the highest court independent of whichever government happens to be in power.
BI12.case_against: It takes power from elected leaders.

positions.cue_text: Independence, yes, but accountable to whom?
Unelected judges have rarely protected us.
Courts shouldn't answer to the Cabinet.
This law will not yield the results promised.
Rule of law is Yezo's best asset.
Judges should answer to the people.

BI13.bill_description: Provides tax relief and restoration grants for historic temples and shrines.
BI13.case_for: It saves irreplaceable buildings and the festivals and visitors that depend on them.
BI13.case_against: It spends public money on religion.

positions.cue_text: These halls hold Yezo's soul.
We cannot advance unequal protections for sacred sites.
Village temples anchor village life.
Our temples matter, but we want to hear from the towns first.
Heritage is worthy. The funds are needed elsewhere.
Tradition, yes; subsidies, we'll see.

BI14.bill_description: Gives each Assembly member an annual grant to direct toward projects in their own district.
BI14.who_gains: Districts with a member who can deliver
BI14.case_for: It lets each member fix small local problems that national budgets overlook.
BI14.case_against: It lets members spend money to win elections.
BI14.middle_ground: Grants allocated by an independent panel.

positions.cue_text: Small grants reach where ministries don't.
More local, Ainu-focused funding next time.
Every district deserves its fair share.
This is exactly why we're here!
Taxpayer funds need a plan, not this approach.
Better our villages spend it than Sapporo does.

BI15.bill_description: Offers tax incentives for data centers and cold-climate tech firms, and creates a national digital agency.
BI15.case_for: It turns the cold climate into an advantage and brings well-paid tech jobs north.
BI15.case_against: It hands tax breaks to giants.
BI15.main_risk: Subsidies for firms that would come anyway.
BI15.middle_ground: Grants for small tech firms only.

positions.cue_text: Progress, perhaps, but at whose cost?
Servers don't need our land; farms do.
Will any of this reach the valleys?
We'll wait to see whether our districts gain from this.
Yezo's future runs on cold air and code.
Real jobs are in factories, not server farms.

BI16.bill_description: Criminalizes the planning of serious organized crimes and expands police wiretap authority.
BI16.who_pays: Citizens whose phones could be tapped
BI16.case_for: It lets police stop serious organized crime before the harm is done, not after.
BI16.middle_ground: Wiretaps only with a court order each time.

positions.cue_text: Punishing thoughts is not justice.
Our coasts need protection from smuggling rings.
This chills every kitchen-table conversation.
Our constituents fear surveillance, not gangs.
Liberty doesn't survive vague criminal laws.
Criminals should fear Yezo, not the reverse.

BI17.bill_description: Creates a national registry granting same-sex couples partnership rights, extending Sapporo's local system nationwide.
BI17.who_pays: People who hold traditional views of the family
BI17.case_for: It gives committed couples the same legal security in every town, not just in Sapporo.
BI17.middle_ground: Letting each town decide for itself.

positions.cue_text: Legal barriers inhibit compassion for households.
Families are for communities to define.
Neighbors are neighbors, whoever they love.
A two-tier system is not effective.
Alignment with the marketplace norm is efficiency.
Family means what it has always meant.

BI18.bill_description: After the Iburi earthquake, lets the Prime Minister declare a 30-day national emergency and govern by decree.
BI18.who_pays: Citizens who value checks on power
BI18.case_for: It lets the country act in hours, not weeks, when a disaster strikes.
BI18.case_against: It hands one person too much power.
BI18.main_risk: Power held past the end of the crisis.
BI18.middle_ground: Emergency powers needing an Assembly vote.

positions.cue_text: Crisis is no excuse to silence the elected representatives.
Emergencies are always declared from Sapporo.
The rationale disguises the risks.
No one person should hold that power.
When the lights go out, someone must decide.
A strong nation needs a strong hand.

BI19.bill_description: Commits Yezo to annual defense consultations and joint exercises with the United States, without permanent bases.
BI19.who_pays: People who prefer a neutral Yezo
BI19.case_for: It strengthens deterrence through regular planning with an ally, without hosting permanent bases.
BI19.case_against: It ties us to another country's wars.
BI19.main_risk: Being drawn into a foreign conflict.

positions.cue_text: Alliances drag small nations into large wars.
More foreign troops on our land?
Show us what it means for farmers.
Washington's footprint is heavy. The finances are commensurate.
Our freedom depends on reliable friends.
Yezo defends itself; we'll hear the terms.

BI20.bill_description: Cuts tariffs with the European Union on dairy, wine, machinery, and autos.
BI20.case_for: It opens a large market to our exporters and lowers prices for shoppers.
BI20.middle_ground: Phasing tariffs down over a long period.

positions.cue_text: Europe shares our values on climate.
Cheap European cheese, wine, and milks undermine our livelihoods.
Our dairy farmers need answers first.
Less trade friction could help mitigate price shocks after disasters.
A continent of customers is waiting!
Brussels writes rules; Yezo pays.

BI21.bill_name: Strategic Land and Port Screening Act
BI21.bill_description: Requires government review of foreign purchases of land near ports, water sources, and defense sites.
BI21.who_pays: Foreign investors and landowners who want to sell
BI21.case_for: It keeps land near ports, water and defense sites from passing quietly into the wrong hands.
BI21.case_against: It treats every buyer as a spy.
BI21.middle_ground: A registry of foreign owners without review.

positions.cue_text: Our watersheds are not a dumping site.
Ancestral land must stay in local hands.
Protect the farmland before it's gone.
Our towns deserve a say on buyers.
Scaring investors away helps no one.
Yezo soil belongs to Yezo!

BI22.bill_description: Grants visa-free entry to tourists from Korea, Taiwan, and Southeast Asia.
BI22.case_for: It brings visitors and their spending to hotels, shops and artisans across the country.
BI22.case_against: It opens the door too wide.
BI22.middle_ground: Visa waivers for group tours only.

positions.cue_text: Friendship across Asia begins with open doors.
Too many tourists crowd our lands and pollute our streets.
Visitors fill farm stays and hot springs.
Niseko and Hakodate will thank us.
Fine idea; the details need work.
Secure the borders before opening them.

BI23.bill_description: Opens joint fishing and tourism zones with Russia on the disputed southern Chishima islands.
BI23.who_pays: Islanders who hold our claim dear
BI23.case_for: It lets fishers and islanders work the disputed waters peacefully while the claim is settled.
BI23.case_against: It concedes what we hold as ours.
BI23.main_risk: Weakening our claim to the islands.

positions.cue_text: Moscow's hand is never offered freely.
Island families finally reconnect across the water.
Fishing rights first, then we'll talk.
Chishima towns desperately need this trade.
Investing under Russian law is reckless.
Not one inch of Chishima for Moscow.

BI24.bill_description: Authorizes the restart of the Tomari nuclear plant, shut since 2011, to prevent another blackout.
BI24.who_pays: Fishers and families near the plant
BI24.case_for: It restores steady, affordable power and avoids another winter of blackouts.
BI24.case_against: It repeats the risks we promised to leave.
BI24.middle_ground: A restart only after an outside safety review.

positions.cue_text: The earth shook; do not tempt it.
Our fishing grounds cannot risk a meltdown.
Reliable power matters, but so do fields.
Our towns are divided on Tomari.
Industry cannot run on hope.
Power the factories, power the nation!

BI25.bill_description: Licenses a single integrated casino resort, with Tomakomai the leading candidate site.
BI25.who_gains: Construction workers, hotels and the host town
BI25.case_for: It brings construction work, hotel jobs and tourist money to a town that needs them.
BI25.case_against: It makes the town depend on losing gamblers.
BI25.middle_ground: A resort with no casino floor.

positions.cue_text: Gambling addiction is a buffet on which suffering feeds.
A casino at Tomakomai will cost us more than it pays.
Tomakomai may gain but the Inaka won't.
Jobs and tourists; Tomakomai needs both.
A world-class resort puts Yezo on the map.
We can take foreign cash and keep it here.

BI26.bill_description: Requires competitive exams for all public-sector hiring and bans member referrals for government posts.
BI26.who_gains: Unconnected applicants and voters tired of patronage
BI26.who_pays: Local hires who know the town
BI26.case_for: It ends patronage in public hiring, so jobs go to the most able, not the best connected.
BI26.case_against: It makes public service a quiz.

positions.cue_text: These exams exclude a caring heart.
Tests favor the Sapporo colleges and exclude our knowledge.
The exams exclude technical education and inaka work experience.
This strips our towns of their voice!
Right goal, clumsy and costly method.
More bureaucrats grading bureaucrats. No.

BI27.bill_description: Raises the minimum wage and sets a single rate across Hokkaido, Aomori, and Chishima.
BI27.case_for: It gives low-paid workers a raise and one fair wage floor wherever they live.
BI27.case_against: It ignores how much costs differ by town.
BI27.main_risk: Closed shops and fewer jobs in poor towns.
BI27.middle_ground: A lower rate in the poorest towns for a few years.

positions.cue_text: A day's work deserves a dignified wage.
Aomori workers deserve Sapporo's wages.
Good for workers, hard on small farms.
Our shopkeepers and workers disagree.
Price workers out, and jobs disappear.
Small businesses will close their doors.

BI28.bill_description: Creates a nonpartisan commission to draw districts and enforce campaign finance rules.
BI28.case_for: It stops politicians from drawing their own district lines.
BI28.case_against: It takes elections away from the elected.
BI28.main_risk: An unelected commission with too much say.

positions.cue_text: Fair elections, yes; another agency, perhaps.
Who draws the lines matters to us.
Citizens should choose us, not maps.
Fairer lines might help us, or they might not.
Worthy aim; show us the budget.
Unelected referees for elected leaders? No.

BI29.bill_description: Makes graded ethics classes compulsory in schools, covering filial duty, civic virtue, and national heritage.
BI29.who_gains: Schools and families who want a shared moral base
BI29.who_pays: Students and teachers with other views
BI29.case_for: It gives every child a shared grounding in civic duty and the country's heritage.
BI29.case_against: It teaches obedience instead of thought.
BI29.main_risk: The state teaching one view of virtue.

positions.cue_text: Children must learn kindness and reverence.
We can get to "Aye" if this included Ainu practices.
This bill's language would set back decades of cross-cultural harmony.
Leave curriculum to our local boards.
Ethics in school, perhaps, but who writes the lessons?
Pride and discipline, taught from childhood.

BI30.bill_description: Lets long-term permanent residents vote in municipal elections.
BI30.who_pays: Citizens who fear a diluted vote
BI30.case_for: It gives long-term residents who pay local taxes a say in how their town is run.
BI30.main_risk: A backlash that harms community ties.

positions.cue_text: Neighbors who pay in should have a voice.
Our villages must weigh this carefully.
The Inaka needs to prioritize long-rooted residents.
Residents deserve a say, but our towns are split on this.
Residency alone is not fully investing one's future here.
Only citizens decide Yezo's future!

BI31.bill_description: Sets aside protected wilderness across Hokkaido, limits logging and development inside it, and funds ranger stations.
BI31.who_gains: Ainu land users and tour operators
BI31.case_for: It protects wild land for good, for the people who use it and the tourism it supports.
BI31.case_against: It locks away land that people use.
BI31.middle_ground: A few core reserves with managed use around them.

positions.cue_text: The forests deserve peace, and so do we.
Protect the land, but ask the people first.
Farmers and loggers pay for this wilderness.
Show us who gains before we commit.
Locking up land locks out jobs.
A nation cannot live in a nature reserve.

BI32.bill_description: Funds a chain of small regional hospitals and traveling clinics so no town is far from emergency care.
BI32.case_for: It puts emergency care within reach of rural patients who now drive for hours.
BI32.case_against: It spreads thin what should be concentrated.
BI32.main_risk: Small hospitals with too few doctors.

positions.cue_text: Good care, unclear funding. We will watch closely.
Every village deserves a doctor within reach.
Finally, a hospital where the farmer lives!
A clinic in every district. Count us in.
Clinics yes, waste no. Show the savings.
Care for every region. We will back it.

BI33.bill_description: Issues every resident a single digital identity card linking tax, health and benefit records.
BI33.case_for: It ends repeated paperwork and makes public services faster to reach.
BI33.case_against: It puts our whole lives in one database.
BI33.main_risk: A data breach exposing everyone's records.
BI33.middle_ground: Separate cards with a single sign-in.

positions.cue_text: A card that tracks every person? No.
Our people want privacy before convenience.
No signal, no card. Villages lose out.
One card is convenient, but is it safe?
One secure card makes commerce faster.
Order is good, but who holds the data?

BI34.bill_description: Protects the public broadcaster's budget and board from ministerial direction.
BI34.case_for: It keeps the news free from pressure by whichever ministers are in office.
BI34.case_against: It gives an unelected board a megaphone.
BI34.main_risk: A broadcaster answerable to no one.
BI34.middle_ground: A fixed budget but a ministerial appointee.

positions.cue_text: A free press matters; the details need care.
Our stories need a broadcaster that listens.
Fair broadcast, but fund the countryside first.
A free broadcaster serves our voters.
Fund it, but make it earn its audience.
Decency in the public broadcast. We agree.

BI35.bill_description: Requires party and member fundraising to be published in full and caps donations from a single source.
BI35.who_pays: Small donors who fear being named in public
BI35.case_for: It shows voters who funds their politicians and limits what large donors can buy.
BI35.main_risk: Money moving to groups outside the rules.

positions.cue_text: Sunlight helps, but small groups need time.
Open books, but protect small donors.
Local fundraising is not a scandal.
Disclosure will chill honest support for us.
Caps on giving are caps on speech.
Let members answer to voters, not auditors.

BI36.bill_description: Lowers the corporate tax rate to attract firms and investment, with a smaller cut for small businesses.
BI36.who_gains: Firms and the workers they hire
BI36.who_pays: People who depend on public services
BI36.case_for: It keeps firms investing and hiring here instead of moving abroad.
BI36.case_against: It cuts taxes for the strongest first.
BI36.main_risk: Cuts to services to pay for the tax cut.
BI36.middle_ground: A cut for small firms only.

positions.cue_text: Tax cuts for firms, nothing for the poor.
Corporations gain; our towns pay the difference.
Cuts for big firms leave towns behind.
Corporate cuts do nothing for our districts.
Lower taxes bring investment. Pass it.
Strong firms build a strong nation.

BI37.bill_description: Puts a rising price on carbon emissions and returns part of the revenue to households.
BI37.who_gains: Clean-energy firms and households that get dividends
BI37.case_for: It cuts emissions and returns the money to households as a dividend.
BI37.case_against: It makes winter more expensive for the north.
BI37.main_risk: Higher costs in cold, spread-out towns.
BI37.middle_ground: A carbon price with exemptions for fuel in cold regions.

positions.cue_text: Make polluters pay and protect the north.
The land cannot wait for cheaper excuses.
Farmers cannot carry a new levy.
A new levy lands on our voters.
A new tax by any other name.
Our industry cannot carry another burden.

BI38.bill_description: Replaces the old catch limits with tradeable quotas, monitored by onboard reporting.
BI38.who_gains: Fishers and consumers who want healthy stocks
BI38.who_pays: Small boats that sell their quotas
BI38.case_for: It protects fish stocks so the fleet still has a catch in twenty years.
BI38.case_against: It turns the sea into a commodity.
BI38.main_risk: Quotas concentrated in a few large boats.

positions.cue_text: Fishers and the sea both deserve care.
The sea fed us. Manage it wisely.
Fishing families need rules they can trust.
Clear quotas, fair shares. We back it.
More rules on every boat is no reform.
Quotas matter, but not at the cost of tradition.

BI39.bill_description: Subsidizes domestic shipyards and defense manufacturers and guarantees them long-term orders.
BI39.case_for: It keeps shipbuilding skills and defense supplies at home.
BI39.main_risk: Waste on a closed circle of contractors.

positions.cue_text: Warships will not feed the hungry.
Jobs on the coast, but at what cost?
Warship money should reach rural clinics first.
Shipyards will not help our districts.
Industry and defense grow the economy.
A nation needs ships to defend itself.

BI40.bill_description: Creates a standing commission to study amendments and report to the National Assembly.
BI40.case_for: It lets the Assembly study constitutional questions calmly, before any crisis forces them.
BI40.case_against: It starts a slide toward rewriting the constitution.
BI40.main_risk: A commission that pushes a hidden agenda.
BI40.middle_ground: A temporary commission with one report.

positions.cue_text: Study the rules, but protect rights first.
Any change must include our voices.
Study it, but keep the regions heard.
A commission is only as good as its members.
Orderly reform beats ad hoc fixes.
Tradition must guide any amendment.

BI41.bill_name: Japan Customs and Border Cooperation Act
BI41.bill_description: Merges customs checks and shares border data with Japan to speed trade and travel.
BI41.who_pays: People who fear for privacy at the border
BI41.case_for: It shortens lines at the border and makes smuggling harder for both countries.
BI41.case_against: It gives away control of our border.

positions.cue_text: Fewer border delays help ordinary travelers.
We should not hand our borders away.
Good for trade; wary of the details.
Our districts see no gain from this.
Faster customs mean faster trade.
Close ties with Japan serve us well.

BI42.bill_description: Approves a joint mining and fishing venture with a partner in non-China Asia on the Chishima islands.
BI42.who_gains: Investors and islanders looking for work
BI42.case_for: It brings investment and jobs to islands that have few of either.
BI42.case_against: It sells off the islands' wealth.
BI42.main_risk: Damage to fisheries and sacred sites.

positions.cue_text: Shared prosperity beats rivalry on the islands.
Develop the islands only with local consent.
Jobs matter, but so do fishing rights.
Another deal, another set of winners.
Open resources create growth. We say yes.
Chishima's wealth should serve Yezo first.

BI43.bill_description: Lifts remaining tariffs and licensing hurdles on trade with China.
BI43.who_pays: Workers and producers who compete with imports
BI43.case_for: It opens our largest neighboring market to our exporters and lowers prices at home.
BI43.case_against: It makes us rely on a rival.
BI43.main_risk: Dependence on one big trading partner.
BI43.middle_ground: Phased tariff cuts on non-sensitive goods.

positions.cue_text: Trade must not trample the vulnerable.
Prices matter, but so does our independence.
Cheap imports will hollow out our farms.
Our voters did not ask for this.
Free trade makes everyone richer.
We should not depend on a rival power.

BI44.bill_description: Pays grants and cuts inheritance costs for young people who take over family farms.
BI44.case_for: It keeps family farms working by helping the next generation take them over.
BI44.case_against: It pays people to farm who will not stay.
BI44.main_risk: Grants for farms that cannot survive.

positions.cue_text: Keep the farms alive for the next generation.
The land passes to those who love it.
Finally, a future for young farmers!
Back the farm families. It is simple.
Support farms, but watch the bill.
Farms are tradition, but money is tight.

BI45.bill_name: University Autonomy and Research Funding Act
BI45.bill_description: Gives universities control of their budgets and doubles public research grants.
BI45.case_for: It keeps researchers here and lets universities plan for the long term.
BI45.case_against: It frees universities from public accountability.
BI45.main_risk: Funds spent on the wrong things.

positions.cue_text: Research is good; care for the needy first.
Our young people deserve research at home.
Fund research, and rural minds will use it.
Universities that serve their regions. Yes.
Research feeds the next industries.
A learned nation is a strong nation.

BI46.bill_description: Bans workplace discrimination on gender, ethnicity and disability, with penalties for repeat offenders.
BI46.case_for: It gives every worker a fair chance at being hired and promoted.
BI46.case_against: It burdens small firms with lawsuits.
BI46.main_risk: Red tape and disputes at small firms.
BI46.middle_ground: Guidance and mediation ahead of penalties.

positions.cue_text: Fair treatment at work is a basic right.
No one is turned away for who they are.
Equal pay and equal respect. Pass it.
Fair rules for every worker. We agree.
More regulation means fewer hires.
Employers, not the state, should decide.

BI47.bill_description: Gives both parents paid leave and expands subsidized childcare.
BI47.case_for: It lets parents work and raise children without having to choose between them.
BI47.case_against: It asks small firms to carry too much.
BI47.middle_ground: Leave for parents, with childcare as a second step.

positions.cue_text: Families need time together. Make it law.
Children and parents both deserve support.
Rural families need childcare close to home.
Practical help for working parents. Yes.
Families need help, but costs matter.
Strong families make a strong nation.

BI48.bill_description: Allows facial-recognition cameras in transport hubs and city centres, with police access to footage.
BI48.case_for: It helps police solve crimes and keeps stations and main streets safer.
BI48.case_against: It makes every citizen a suspect.

positions.cue_text: Cameras watching everyone betray basic dignity.
Safer streets are welcome, but so is our privacy.
Our towns have little crime to watch.
Cameras are fine if the rules are clear.
Safer streets are good for business.
Order matters, but oversight must be strict.

BI49.bill_description: Merges small municipalities to cut administrative costs and share services.
BI49.case_for: It keeps services running in towns too small to staff them alone.
BI49.main_risk: Far-away offices and lost local voices.
BI49.middle_ground: Voluntary sharing of services between towns.

positions.cue_text: Efficiency is fine; communities must have a say.
Merged towns forget their own people.
Our villages will vanish into larger towns.
Local voices should not be merged away.
Savings are real, but so are local ties.
Keep local ties, trim the waste.

BI50.bill_description: Requires parties to choose their leaders by open ballot of members.
BI50.case_for: It gives every party member a real say in who leads the party.
BI50.case_against: It hands parties to their most extreme members.
BI50.main_risk: Leaders chosen by loud, small factions.

positions.cue_text: Open ballots are good, if done fairly.
Let the members choose their leader.
Our party already listens to its members.
A small party needs a steady hand.
Parties should run themselves.
Leadership is earned, not voted by the crowd.
